newsitem.title: CHINA: China says needs grain stocks at least 75 mln T.
newsitem.headline: China says needs grain stocks at least 75 mln T.

text.p: China should keep its state grain reserves at no less than 75 million tonnes to meet possible shortfalls, the Grain and Oils Market Daily said on Thursday.
The reserve level should be equivalent to two months of national consumption, it quoted Wang Lingui of the State Grain Reserves Administration as saying.
Of the total reserves, grain reserves held by the central government should be no less than 40 million tonnes, he said.
China releases about 15 million tonnes of grain each year from state reserves to meet shortages caused by natural disasters, he said.
China's state grain reserves totalled 148.5 million tonnes at the end of 1996, Vice Premier Zhu Rongji said last month.
The reserves had previously been kept as a state secret.
